text:
maria: quick q — product wants a 99.9% latency SLO for Console API derived from traces. what's the recommended pipeline here? keep full spans for X days? export histograms to metrics? worried about cost + tail accuracy. cc @jon @ashley
jon: i'd avoid doing SLO math directly in the tracing DB. cheaper and more reliable to export latency histograms to our metrics backend and compute SLOs there, with exemplars pointing back to traces for debugging. keep raw spans shorter retention.
ashley: +1. also watch cardinality. if you tag by full request path + customer-id you'll blow up storage. limit aggregation keys to: route, model_family, customer_tier.
ryan: to add — use tail sampling to keep a small fraction of slow traces and full traces for errors. then export aggregate histograms (HDR or tdigest) from the collector, e.g.:
```yaml
exporters:
  prometheus:
    endpoint: 0.0.0.0:9464
processors:
  batch:
  memory_limiter:
  tail_sampling:
    policies:
      - name: slow_traces
        type: latency
        latency: 500ms
        sample_rate: 0.02
```
jon: nice. also enable exemplars so metrics -> trace link works: prometheus_remote_write + exemplars. that way a spike in latency has a trace to inspect.
ashley: retention numbers I'd propose: raw spans 14–30d (configurable per-customer), aggregated histograms 90d, metrics 365d. do a cost-model run before increasing spans retention.
maria: how do we compute the 99.9% from histograms reliably? percentile approximation issues on downsampled traces?
ryan: compute from exported histograms (bucketed) in metrics—Prometheus supports histogram_quantile on aggregated histograms if buckets are consistent. use high-res buckets for the tail (e.g., exponential buckets up to 10s). keep a fallback: use traces for exact tail during incident investigations via exemplars.
jon: metrics-based SLOs also let us compute error budgets and burn rates efficiently (sliding windows). then we can feed those alerts into Console dashboards and routing policies.
ashley: note: if you use tail-sampling, calculate sampling bias correction when projecting percentiles. or prefer collector-side histogram aggregation (no bias) if possible.
maria: action items?
jon: i'll prepare a dashboard template with: p99/p99.9 latency (by route), error budget burn, exemplar links.
ashley: i'll prototype an otel-collector config and run the storage/cost estimate for 14d vs 30d spans.
ryan: i'll draft alert rules for SLO burn and a snippet to compute quantiles from histogram buckets.
infra-bot: scheduled job "otel-collector/config-test" started by ashley at 2026-03-12T15:40:00Z :gear:
maria: awesome — thanks team. once we have cost numbers let's pick retention defaults and rollout plan (canary on dev + one small customer). :thumbsup:
